subject: science
passage: Many people grow up believing that the sky is blue because it reflects the color of the oceans, which cover most of Earth's surface. The idea seems sensible, since the sky and the sea often appear to be similar shades.
passage_b: Physicists explain the blue sky without the oceans at all. Sunlight contains all colors, and as it passes through the atmosphere, tiny molecules of air scatter the shorter, bluer wavelengths far more than the red ones. This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from every direction, which is why the sky looks blue even over deserts far from any sea.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the belief in Text 1?

choices.A: By claiming that sunlight contains only blue and red wavelengths
choices.B: By arguing that the sky is not really blue but appears blue only over the sea
choices.C: By explaining that the sky's color comes from the way air scatters sunlight
choices.D: By agreeing that the oceans give the sky its blue color

explanation.why: Text 1 describes the belief that the sky is blue because it reflects the oceans. Text 2 says physicists explain the color "without the oceans at all": air molecules scatter blue light most, so the sky is blue "even over deserts far from any sea." Text 2 replaces the belief with a different explanation.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says sunlight "contains all colors," not only blue and red.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says the sky looks blue "even over deserts far from any sea," the opposite of this choice.
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 explains that air molecules scatter blue light more than red light, which makes the sky look blue.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 explains the sky's color "without the oceans at all," so it would not agree.
